results.title: The Gram matrices of a bilinear form in two bases have the same rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, let $B$ be a bilinear form on $V$, and let $b = (b_i)_{i \in n_1}$ and $c = (c_j)_{j \in n_2}$ be bases of $V$ indexed by finite types $n_1$ and $n_2$. Then the Gram matrices $(B(b_i, b_j))_{i, j \in n_1}$ and $(B(c_i, c_j))_{i, j \in n_2}$ have the same rank.

results.title: Rank of a bilinear form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, let $B$ be a bilinear form on $V$, and let $b = (b_i)_{i \in n}$ be a basis of $V$ indexed by a finite type $n$. The rank of $B$ with respect to $b$ is the rank of the Gram matrix $(B(b_i, b_j))_{i, j \in n}$ of $B$ in $b$.

results.title: Rank of a bilinear form via its Gram matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, let $B$ be a bilinear form on $V$, and let $b = (b_i)_{i \in n}$ be a basis of $V$ indexed by a finite type $n$. Then the rank of $B$ with respect to $b$ equals the rank of the Gram matrix $(B(b_i, b_j))_{i, j \in n}$. This holds by definition.

results.title: Basis independence of the rank of a bilinear form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$, let $B$ be a bilinear form on $V$, and let $b = (b_i)_{i \in n_1}$ and $c = (c_j)_{j \in n_2}$ be bases of $V$ indexed by finite types $n_1$ and $n_2$. Then the rank of $B$ with respect to $b$ equals the rank of the Gram matrix $(B(c_i, c_j))_{i, j \in n_2}$ of $B$ in $c$.

results.title: Warren–Bray congruence for prime divisors of Fermat numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$ be the $n$-th Fermat number. For every $n \ge 2$ and every odd prime $p$ dividing $F_n$, we have $2^{(p-1)/2} \equiv 1 \pmod{F_n}$. This result is due to Warren and Bray (1967).

results.title: Squared prime factors of Fermat numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$ be the $n$-th Fermat number, and let $p$ be a prime dividing $F_n$. Then $p^2$ divides $F_n$ if and only if $2^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$.

results.title: Squared prime factors of Fermat numbers via Wieferich primes and orders
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$ be the $n$-th Fermat number. For every natural number $n$ and every odd prime $p$, $p^2$ divides $F_n$ if and only if $p$ is a Wieferich prime (to base $2$) and the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo $p$ is $2^{n+1}$.

results.title: Greatest common divisors of generalized Fermat numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $k$ write $F_k(a, b) = a^{b^k} + 1$, and let $a, b \ge 2$ and $m$, $n$ be natural numbers. If $n < m$ and $a$ and $b$ are both even, then $\gcd(F_m(a, b), F_n(a, b)) = 1$. If $n < m$, $a$ is odd and $b$ is even, then $\gcd(F_m(a, b), F_n(a, b)) = 2$. If $n \le m$ and $b$ is odd, then $\gcd(F_m(a, b), F_n(a, b)) = F_n(a, b)$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the number of prime factors of generalized Fermat numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $n$ write $F_n(a, b) = a^{b^n} + 1$, and let $\Omega(N)$ be the number of prime factors of $N$ counted with multiplicity. If $a, b \ge 2$ and $b$ is odd, then $\Omega(F_n(a, b)) \le \Omega(F_m(a, b))$ for all natural numbers $n \le m$.

results.title: Smaller iterated powers are not congruent to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a, b, m \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$ be natural numbers with $a^{b^n} \not\equiv 1 \pmod m$. Then $a^{b^t} \not\equiv 1 \pmod m$ for every natural number $t < n$.

results.title: Log-concave densities
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is a log-concave density when it is measurable, $f(x) \ge 0$ for every $x$, and $f(x)^{1-t} f(y)^t \le f((1-t)x + ty)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and every real $t$ with $0 < t < 1$.

results.title: Isotropic log-concave probability measures
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is isotropic log-concave when it is a probability measure, it has density $f$ with respect to Lebesgue measure for some log-concave density $f$, and for all coordinates $i, j$ the functions $x \mapsto x_i$ and $x \mapsto x_i x_j$ are $\mu$-integrable with $\int x_i \, d\mu(x) = 0$ and $\int x_i x_j \, d\mu(x) = \delta_{ij}$, that is, $1$ if $i = j$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Normalized radius variance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the normalized radius variance of $\mu$ is $\frac{1}{n} \int (\|x\|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$, computed in $[0, \infty]$, where $\|x\|$ is the Euclidean norm (for $n = 0$ the integral is $0$ and so is the value).

results.title: Thin-shell variance constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write $|x|$ for the Euclidean norm. The thin-shell variance constant is the supremum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of the normalized radius variance $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ over all dimensions $n \ge 1$ and all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Thin-shell width
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write $|x|$ for the Euclidean norm. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the thin-shell width in dimension $n$ is the square root of the supremum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of $\int (|x| - \sqrt{n})^2 \, d\mu(x)$ over all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $\sqrt{\infty} = \infty$.

results.title: Elementary radius deviation bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all real numbers $r \ge 0$ and $d > 0$, $(r - \sqrt{d})^2 \le (r^2 - d)^2 / d$.

results.title: Radius fluctuation is bounded by the normalized radius variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n > 0$ and every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the integral $\int (\|x\| - \sqrt{n})^2 \, d\mu(x)$, taken in $[0, \infty]$ with $\|x\|$ the Euclidean norm, is at most the normalized radius variance of $\mu$.

results.title: The thin-shell variance constant bounds the normalized radius variance of isotropic log-concave measures
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The thin-shell variance constant bounds the normalized radius variance of isotropic log-concave measures. For every $n > 0$ and every isotropic log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the normalized radius variance of $\mu$ is at most the thin-shell variance constant.

results.title: Characterization of bounds on the thin-shell variance constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $C \in [0, \infty]$, the thin-shell variance constant is at most $C$ if and only if, for every $n > 0$ and every isotropic log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the normalized radius variance of $\mu$ is at most $C$.

results.title: The thin-shell variance constant bounds the radius fluctuation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n > 0$ and every isotropic log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the integral $\int (\|x\| - \sqrt{n})^2 \, d\mu(x)$, taken in $[0, \infty]$ with $\|x\|$ the Euclidean norm, is at most the thin-shell variance constant.

results.title: The thin-shell variance constant is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The thin-shell variance constant, a value in $[0, \infty]$, is at least $0$.

results.title: Thin-shell width is at most the square root of the variance constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every dimension $n \ge 1$, the thin-shell width in dimension $n$ is at most the square root of the thin-shell variance constant, computed in $[0, \infty]$ with $\sqrt{\infty} = \infty$.

results.title: A uniform variance bound makes the thin-shell variance constant finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $C$ is a real number such that for every $n > 0$ and every isotropic log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ the normalized radius variance of $\mu$ is at most $\max(C, 0)$, then the thin-shell variance constant is finite.

results.title: Klartag's first thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C \sqrt{n / \log n}$.

results.title: Klartag's power-law thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a constant $C > 0$ and an integer $N \ge 3$ such that for every dimension $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C n^{2/5 + \varepsilon}$. Here $\sigma_n$ is the square root of the supremum of $\mathbb{E}\,(|X| - \sqrt{n})^2$ over isotropic log-concave random vectors $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Fleury's thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C n^{3/8}$.

results.title: Guédon–Milman thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C n^{1/3}$.

results.title: Lee–Vempala thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a constant $C > 0$ and an integer $N \ge 3$ such that for every dimension $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C n^{1/4}$. Here $\sigma_n$ is the square root of the supremum of $\mathbb{E}\,(|X| - \sqrt{n})^2$ over isotropic log-concave random vectors $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Chen's thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le \exp\big((\log n)^{1/2 + \varepsilon}\big)$.

results.title: Klartag–Lehec polylogarithmic thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C (\log n)^4$.

results.title: Jambulapati–Lee–Vempala thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha = \big(1 + 7\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{53 - 4\sqrt{2}}\big)/8$. There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C (\log n)^{\alpha}$.

results.title: Klartag's square-root-logarithmic thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a constant $C > 0$ and an integer $N \ge 3$ such that for every dimension $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C \sqrt{\log n}$. Here $\sigma_n$ is the square root of the supremum of $\mathbb{E}\,(|X| - \sqrt{n})^2$ over isotropic log-concave random vectors $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Guan's thin-shell bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C \log \log n$.

results.title: Klartag–Lehec thin-shell variance bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a real $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n \ge 1$ and every isotropic log-concave measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the normalized radius variance $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ is at most $C$.

results.title: Klartag–Lehec bounded thin-shell width
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a real $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n \ge 1$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C$.

results.title: The thin-shell variance constant is finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The thin-shell variance constant, the supremum in $[0, \infty]$ of the normalized radius variances $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ over all dimensions $n \ge 1$ and all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, is finite.

results.title: The standard Gaussian has normalized radius variance 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every dimension $n \ge 1$, the standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is isotropic log-concave (a probability measure with a log-concave Lebesgue density, mean $0$ and identity covariance), and its normalized radius variance $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\gamma_n(x)$ equals $2$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The thin-shell variance constant, an element of $[0, \infty]$, is at least $4/5$.

results.title: The thin-shell variance constant is at least 2

results.summary: The thin-shell variance constant, the supremum in $[0, \infty]$ of the normalized radius variances $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ over all dimensions $n \ge 1$ and all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, is at least $2$.

results.title: Schnirelmann's inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a set $A$ of natural numbers, let $\sigma(A) = \inf_{n \ge 1} |A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| / n$ be its Schnirelmann density. If $A$ and $B$ are sets of natural numbers that both contain $0$, then their sumset $A + B = \{a + b : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$ satisfies $\sigma(A) + \sigma(B) - \sigma(A)\sigma(B) \le \sigma(A + B)$.

results.title: Schnirelmann's basis theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a set of natural numbers with $0 \in A$ whose Schnirelmann density $\sigma(A) = \inf_{n \ge 1} |A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| / n$ is positive. Then $A$ is an additive basis of finite order: there is a natural number $h$ such that every natural number $n$ can be written as $n = a_1 + \dots + a_h$ with $a_1, \dots, a_h \in A$, repetitions allowed.

results.title: Unary code of an index
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The code of an index $i \in \mathbb{N}$ is the bit word $\mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ of length $i + 1$: the bit $\mathbf{t}$ (true) followed by $i$ copies of the bit $\mathbf{f}$ (false); with $|$ for true and $1$ for false, it is the word $|\,1^i$.

results.title: Concatenated code of an index sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite sequence $I = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$ of natural numbers, its code is the bit word $c(i_1)\,c(i_2) \cdots c(i_n)$, the concatenation of the unary codes $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ of its entries; the empty sequence has the empty code.

results.title: List word of an index sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P = (d_0, \dots, d_{m-1})$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$, let $s$ be a function sending each domino to a word over $\alpha$, and set $w_i = s(d_i)$ for $i < m$ and $w_i = s(\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ for $i \ge m$, where $(\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ is the domino with empty top and bottom. The list word of an index sequence $i_1, \dots, i_n$ is the word $w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_n}\, c(i_n) \cdots c(i_1)$…

results.title: List language of a PCP instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P = (d_0, \dots, d_{m-1})$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$, let $s$ be a function sending each domino to a word over $\alpha$ (for instance its top word), and write $w_i = s(d_i)$. The list language of $s$ and $P$ is the language over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ of all words $w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_n}\, c(i_n) \cdots c(i_1)$ with $n \ge 1$ and $i_1, \dots, i_n < m$, where $c(i)$ is the unary code of $i$:…

results.title: Concatenated index codes are uniquely decodable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite sequence $I = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$ of natural numbers write $c(I) = c(i_1) \cdots c(i_n)$, where $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ is the unary code of $i$. If $I$ and $J$ are finite sequences of natural numbers with $c(I) = c(J)$, then $I = J$.

results.title: A PCP instance is solvable exactly when its top and bottom list languages meet
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A list $P$ of dominoes has a PCP solution if and only if some word belongs both to the list language of the top words of $P$ and to the list language of the bottom words of $P$.

results.title: Encoded nonterminal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ and a natural number $A$, the nonterminal $A$ as a symbol of an encoded grammar over the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$, that is, the element $\mathrm{inl}\, A$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.

results.title: Encoded letter terminal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a letter $a \in \alpha$, the terminal $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ as a symbol of an encoded grammar, that is, the element $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{inl}\, a)$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.

results.title: Encoded bit terminal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ and a bit $b$, the terminal $b$ of the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ as a symbol of an encoded grammar, that is, the element $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{inr}\, b)$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.

results.title: List of all letters
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite alphabet $\alpha$, the list of all letters of $\alpha$, each appearing exactly once, in some fixed but unspecified order.

results.title: The letters other than a given letter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a letter $a$ of a finite alphabet with decidable equality, the list of all letters $b$ of the alphabet with $b \ne a$, in the order of a fixed enumeration of the alphabet.

results.title: Domino-independent productions of the universality grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite alphabet $\alpha$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is a list of productions whose nonterminals $N_0, N_1, \dots$ are encoded as natural numbers and whose terminals are the letters $a \in \alpha$ and the two bits $\mathbf{t}$ (true) and $\mathbf{f}$ (false). Writing $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ for the unary code of an index $i$, the list consists of the productions $N_3 \to \varepsilon$,…

results.title: The mismatch productions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mismatch productions of a nonterminal $A$ for one side of a list $P$ of dominoes over a finite alphabet. Let $s$ be a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom). For each index $i < |P|$ write $w = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$ and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ for the unary code of $i$ as bits. results.title: The universality grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the encoded context-free grammar over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ with start nonterminal $0$ whose productions are the base productions for $k = |P|$, followed by the mismatch productions of the top words of $P$ with nonterminal $1$, followed by the mismatch productions of the bottom words of $P$ with nonterminal $2$.

results.title: Words of letters
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language of words of letters is the set of all words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ whose symbols all lie in $\alpha$, that is, the words over $\alpha$ (including the empty word) viewed as words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$.

results.title: Nonempty words of letters
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language of nonempty words of letters is the set of all nonempty words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ whose symbols all lie in $\alpha$, that is, the nonempty words over $\alpha$ viewed as words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$.

results.title: Words of bits
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language over the disjoint union of $\alpha$ and the bits $\{\mathbf{t}, \mathbf{f}\}$ consisting of the words in which every symbol is a bit, including the empty word.

results.title: Codes of index sequences below $k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the language over the disjoint union of $\alpha$ and the bits $\{\mathbf{t}, \mathbf{f}\}$ consisting of the bit words $c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$ with $n \ge 0$ and $j_1, \dots, j_n < k$, where $c(j) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^j$ is the unary code of $j$. In particular it contains the empty word.

results.title: The mismatch language
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mismatch language of one side of a list $P$ of dominoes. Let $s$ be a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom), write $w_i = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$ and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ for the unary code of $i$ as bits. The language, over letters and bits, consists of the words $x\,\mathrm{code}(i_n) \cdots \mathrm{code}(i_1)$ where $x$ is a word of letters and $i_1, \dots, i_n$ with…

results.title: Malformed words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Consider words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$, whose symbols are letters from $\alpha$ and bits, and read the bit $\mathrm{true}$ as the separator $|$ and the bit $\mathrm{false}$ as $1$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a word is malformed with bound $k$ when at least one of the following holds: it consists of letters only (possibly none); it is a word of letters followed by a nonempty word of bits whose first bit is…

results.title: Intended languages of the nonterminals of the universality grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the assignment of a language over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ to each natural number that sends $0$ to the union of the malformed language for $k = |P|$ and the mismatch languages of the top words and of the bottom words of $P$; $1$ to the mismatch language of the top words of $P$; $2$ to the mismatch language of the bottom words of $P$; $3$ to the words of letters; $4$…

results.title: Evaluating a form with one nonterminal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ assign a language over $T$ to each nonterminal. For terminal words $u$ and $v$, a nonterminal $A$ and a word $w$, the word $w$ lies in the language that $V$ assigns to the sentential form $u\,A\,v$ if and only if $w = u z v$ for some $z \in V(A)$.

results.title: Evaluating a form with two nonterminals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ assign a language over $T$ to each nonterminal. For terminal words $u$, $v$ and $x$, nonterminals $A$ and $B$ and a word $w$, the word $w$ lies in the language that $V$ assigns to the sentential form $u\,A\,v\,B\,x$ if and only if $w = u z_1 v z_2 x$ for some $z_1 \in V(A)$ and $z_2 \in V(B)$.

results.title: The intended languages form a valuation of the universality grammar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality and let $P$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$. The assignment of intended languages to the nonterminals of the universality grammar of $P$ is a valuation of that grammar: for every production $A \to \gamma$, the language that $\gamma$ denotes under the assignment is contained in the language assigned to $A$.

results.title: A word that does not start with $w$ leaves $w$ at some position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $w$ and $x$ be words over an alphabet $\alpha$ such that $w$ is not a prefix of $x$. Then there is a position $m < |w|$ with the following property: writing $w = u\,c\,r$ with $|u| = m$ and $c \in \alpha$, either $x = u$, or $x = u\,a\,y$ for some letter $a \ne c$ and some word $y$.

results.title: No right symbol directly precedes a left symbol in a left-then-right word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types and consider words over the disjoint union $\alpha \sqcup \beta$. For all words $u, v$ over $\alpha \sqcup \beta$, all $b \in \beta$ and $a \in \alpha$, all words $X$ over $\alpha$ and all words $Y$ over $\beta$, we have $u\,b\,a\,v \ne X\,Y$: a word over $\alpha$ followed by a word over $\beta$ never has a symbol of $\beta$ immediately followed by a symbol of $\alpha$.

results.title: A bit inside a word of letters followed by bits starts a suffix of the bits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types, call the elements of $\alpha$ letters and those of $\beta$ bits, and regard words over $\alpha$ and over $\beta$ as words over the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$. If $u\,b\,z = X\,Y$ for words $u, z$ over $\alpha \oplus \beta$, a bit $b$, a word $X$ of letters and a word $Y$ of bits, then there are words $Y_1, Y_2$ of bits with $Y = Y_1 Y_2$ and $b\,z = Y_2$.

results.title: Codes of indices below $k$ contain no code of $k$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $J = (j_1, \dots, j_n)$ be a finite sequence of natural numbers with $j_1, \dots, j_n < k$. Write $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ for the unary code of $i$ and $c(J) = c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$. Then there are no bit words $Y$ and $Z$ with $c(J) = Y\,c(k)\,Z$.

results.title: Mismatched words are not in the list language
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a list of dominoes and $s$ a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom). No word of the mismatch language of $s$ for $P$ belongs to the list language of $s$ for $P$.

results.title: Every word is malformed or well formed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $w$ be a word over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$. Then $w$ is malformed with bound $k$, or $w = x\, c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$ for a word $x$ over $\alpha$ and a nonempty sequence of indices $j_1, \dots, j_n < k$, where $c(j)$ is the unary code of $j$: the bit $\mathrm{true}$ followed by $j$ bits $\mathrm{false}$.

results.title: The universality grammar generates every word exactly when PCP has no solution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality and let $P$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$. The universality grammar of $P$ generates every word over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ if and only if the Post correspondence problem $P$ has no solution.

results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A single copy-number event on a region: `copies` original copies, of which copy `i` has `desc i` copies after the event (`0` if lost, `2` if duplicated).

results.title: Copy number after a copy-number event
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The copy number `c₁ = ∑ i, desc i` after the event.

results.title: Number of amplified copies
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of original copies amplified by the event (`desc i ≥ 2`).

results.title: Expected number of mutations of a given multiplicity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Expected number of mutations of multiplicity `m`: `μ t #{i | desc i = m} + [m = 1] μ c₁ (1 - t)` (per-copy rate `μ`, event at time `t` of the normalized history `[0, 1]`).

results.title: The multiplicity-weighted total is time-invariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `∑_m m E_m = μ c₁`, summing over all multiplicities up to a bound `B ≥ max(1, max_i desc i)`.

results.summary: When some copy is amplified and `μ ≠ 0`, `t = c₁ ∑_{m ≥ 2} E_m / (#{i | desc i ≥ 2} ∑_m m E_m)`.
